Create a CRUK-branded table

Source: R/crukTable.R
crukTable.Rd

Builds a reactable::reactable() widget with CRUK styling. All styling comes from inst/www/css/tables.css, which is attached as an HTML dependency. In a Shiny app you will usually use crukTableOutput() in the UI and renderCrukTable() in the server instead of calling this directly. Call it directly in R Markdown, Quarto, or for static tables.

Usage

crukTable(
  data,
  columns = NULL,
  sortable = TRUE,
  filterable = FALSE,
  selection = "multiple",
  onClick = if (!is.null(selection)) "select" else NULL,
  highlight = TRUE,
  pagination = FALSE,
  defaultPageSize = NULL,
  class = NULL,
  WindowSize = NULL,
  mobileBreakpoint = 900,
  mobileMaxWidth = 375,
  mobile = NULL,
  fitHeaders = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

data

A data frame or matrix to display.

columns

Optional named list of column definitions created with reactable::colDef(). A column that sets any of width, maxWidth or minWidth keeps exactly that sizing; see fitHeaders.

sortable

Logical. Whether columns can be sorted by clicking the column headers. Default is TRUE.

filterable

Logical. Whether filter inputs are displayed for columns. Default is FALSE.

selection

Row selection mode: "multiple", "single", or NULL for no selection. Default is "multiple". Rows are selected by clicking them; reactable's checkbox column is not shown (and takes up no space). To show it anyway, supply your own .selection column definition in columns.

onClick

Action to perform when a row is clicked. Defaults to "select" when selection is set, otherwise NULL.

highlight

Logical. Whether rows are highlighted on hover. Default is TRUE.

pagination

Logical. Whether pagination is enabled. Default is FALSE, unless defaultPageSize is supplied and pagination is not, in which case pagination is switched on.

defaultPageSize

Number of rows per page. If NULL, all rows are shown when pagination is off and 10 when it is on. Supplying a page size switches pagination on unless you also set pagination = FALSE, in which case the page size is ignored (with a warning).

class

Optional extra CSS class(es) for the table.

WindowSize

Optional. The current window size, i.e. the value of the reactive returned by window_size_server(): pass WindowSize(), not WindowSize. Any list with a numeric width element works. When the window is narrower than mobileBreakpoint, a compact version of the table is drawn: smaller fonts and cell padding, and a smaller default minimum column width so that the table is about mobileMaxWidth pixels wide or less. If NULL (the default), or the width is not yet known, the full-size table is drawn. Call crukTable() inside renderCrukTable() so the table redraws when the window is resized. Note that a redraw resets sorting, filtering and selection. Any width, minWidth or maxWidth you set in columns takes precedence over the compact defaults. Passing WindowSize = win_size() inside renderCrukTable() redraws the table on every window size update, which resets the current page. Prefer mobile = window_is_narrow(win_size) (see below) in Shiny apps.

mobileBreakpoint

Window width in pixels below which the compact table is used. Default is 900 (Bootstrap's md breakpoint). Only used with WindowSize; with mobile, the breakpoint is whatever you gave window_is_narrow().

mobileMaxWidth

Target maximum table width in pixels for the compact table. Used to work out the default minimum column width (the table width is not capped if there are too many columns to fit; it then scrolls horizontally inside its container). Default is 375. With fitHeaders = TRUE a column is never made narrower than its longest header word, so this is a target rather than a guarantee: tables with long headers or many columns will scroll horizontally on small screens rather than shrink the text or split words.

mobile

Optional. TRUE or FALSE: draw the compact version of the table (see WindowSize) or the full-size one. In a Shiny app, pass the reactive from window_is_narrow() called, i.e. mobile = is_narrow(). Because window_is_narrow() only changes when the window crosses its breakpoint, the table is redrawn only then, rather than on every resize, so the current page, sort order and selection are kept. If supplied, mobile takes precedence over WindowSize. If NULL (the default), WindowSize is used.

fitHeaders

Logical. If TRUE (the default), each column's minimum width is raised, if necessary, so that the longest word in its header fits on one line instead of being split mid-word. The width is estimated from the number of characters (not measured in the browser), and capped so that one very long word cannot make a column huge. Columns are left alone if their colDef() sets width, maxWidth or minWidth, or sets show = FALSE or a custom header. Set to FALSE for reactable's own sizing.

...

Additional arguments passed to reactable::reactable().

Value

A reactable htmlwidget with the CRUK table stylesheet attached.

See also

crukTableOutput(), renderCrukTable(), window_is_narrow()

Examples

crukTable(head(mtcars), filterable = FALSE, selection = NULL)



# Force the compact version
crukTable(head(mtcars), mobile = TRUE)



if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# In a Shiny app: redraw only when the window crosses the breakpoint
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  win_size  <- window_size_server("window_tracker")
  is_narrow <- window_is_narrow(win_size, breakpoint = 900)

  output$table <- renderCrukTable(
    crukTable(mtcars, pagination = TRUE, mobile = is_narrow())
  )
}
} # }
